generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

traits.note: Accounts of the family by Michigan State's Botany Online and the University of Hawaii (G. Carr), as search results quote them (the pages themselves were not read): tepals 6, alike, in two whorls of 3; stamens usually 6 (rarely 3, 4 or up to 12); ovary superior, of 3 fused carpels, one style with a 3-lobed stigma.

traits.leaf_division.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 372 Liliaceae, of which APG keeps the lilies, tulips, fritillaries and their kin: leaves simple; fruit a capsule opening along or between its cells, or a fleshy berry (the berries in Clintonia and Streptopus).

traits.fruit_type.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 372 Liliaceae, of which APG keeps the lilies, tulips, fritillaries and their kin: leaves simple; fruit a capsule opening along or between its cells, or a fleshy berry (the berries in Clintonia and Streptopus).

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 218, 221, 222, family Liliaceae: leaf arrangement alternate (spiral), usually; read as {"alternate": "usually"}.

traits.leaf_venation.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 218, 221, 222, family Liliaceae: leaf venation parallel (rarely net-veined), usually; read as {"parallel": "usually"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 218, 221, 222, family Liliaceae: inflorescence terminal raceme or solitary (rarely umbel), usually; read as {"raceme": "often", "solitary": "often"}.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 218, 221, 222, family Liliaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite; read as "hermaphrodite".

traits.life_span.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 218, 221, 222, family Liliaceae: life span perennial; read as "perennial".
